missing.what_was_said: Management expected non-AI execution challenges to affect H2. It also expected AI capacity constraints in Q3, but supply to be roughly in line with near-term demand by FY2025-end.

Azure grew 35% in constant currency, including 16 percentage points from AI services, and AI capacity came online faster than expected. Nevertheless, faster-growing demand meant AI capacity constraints were now expected beyond June.

Management said Azure's 39% growth significantly exceeded expectations, driven by accelerated core infrastructure growth primarily from its largest customers. Additional datacenter capacity came online, but demand remained higher than supply.

missing.what_was_said: Management said, “Outside of this useful life impact, our calendar year 2026 CapEx investment expectations remain unchanged.” It also clarified that finance leases are included in capital expenditures while operating leases are not, distinguishing the accounting-driven revision from a cut to underlying investment plans.

Management expected capex to accelerate in the second half of FY2027, driven by CPUs, higher memory and storage costs, GPUs, and third-party capacity deliveries that had shifted into that period. This qualified the lower CY2026 guidance as partly a timing shift.
